Measures have been put in place to ensure that only authorized personnel are on the factory premises at any point in time. This includes visitors on site. 7.2.3.2 This establishment has in place at least one of the following measures for personnel security; 7.2.3.2.1 Employee Security 7.2.3.2.1.1 During hiring of employees, thorough background checks are done. 7.2.3.2.1.2 Employees are trained to know what they can do on site. 7.2.3.2.1.3 Areas restricted to be accessed by only a category of employees is made known to every employee hired. 7.2.3.2.1.4 Confidentiality clauses are inserted into employment letters. Employees are made to sign the confidentiality agreement. 7.2.3.2.2 Non-employee Security 7.2.3.2.2.1 Provision has been made for non-employees such as visitors, guests, customers, contractors, suppliers, third party drivers etc. 7.2.3.2.2.2 A log of non-employees entering the establishment is maintained at the main security area. 7.2.3.2.2.3 A visitor’s ID card has been designed with numbers and these are assigned to every visitor who enters the facility to conduct one business or the other. 7.2.3.2.2.4 All visitors are mandated to wear their visitor ID cards where they would be very visible. 7.2.3.2.2.5 Non-employees are chaperoned on-site by security or the person they came to transact business with and they are basically restricted to designated areas of the factory. 7.2.3.2.2.6 Non-employees have restrictions on what they can do on site. For instance, non-employees are not permitted to take pictures on site. 7.2.3.2.3 Security Training 7.2.3.2.3.1 All new employees undergo security awareness training. Existing employees undergo periodic security awareness training. 7.2.3.2.3.2 Employees are trained on access control, handling of sensitive information, what suspicious activities look like and reporting such activities to management or the security team. 7.2.4 Incident Response Security Measures. 7.2.4.1 An incident response security references the incident management plan already in place. The idea is to respond quickly to a product contamination threat or event using planned measures. 7.2.4.2 There is already an existing incident management plan which deals with product recalls whether it is food safety related or quality

One measure to ensure safety of incoming and outgoing materials is ensuring that suppliers secure loads with seals. 7.2.1.3.2.3 All trucks leaving the factory with finished products or packaging materials for outside storage are sealed/or shrink-wrapped. 7.2.1.3.3 Mail Handling Security 7.2.1.3.3.1 All parcels and letters coming through the mail or hand-delivered are handled away from the production floor, canteen, finished goods warehouse, packaging stores and any other place on site which is close to products, packaging or the production areas. 7.2.1.3.3.1 All employees who handle mail are trained on bioterrorism and how to handle items of external origin. 7.2.2. Inside Security Measures 7.2.2.1 Measures are taken within the perimeter including offices and production areas to ensure security is maintained. 7.2.2.2 Access control has been incorporated into door lock systems to give access to only authorized persons to specific areas of the factory. 7.2.2.3 Signs have been posted at areas to clearly communicate restricted access status. The main purpose of these activities is to protect product from intentional contamination. 7.2.2.4 Access to the raw paper storage and printing inks for instance is restricted. All access points are locked and only authorized personnel have access to it. 7.2.2.5 This establishment has in place at least one of the following measures for inside security. 7.2.2.5.1 General Inside Security 7.2.2.5.1.1 Any parcel that raises suspicion is reported to the security team. 7.2.2.5.1.2 All restricted areas within the factory are clearly identified and labelled as such. 7.2.2.5.1.3 Any material which is suspected not to have been previously inspected is quarantined for thorough inspection before use.

| 4 | Waste Disposal | PRP for Waste Disposal | The purpose of this PRP is to outline the procedure for managing waste on site to maintain a sanitary/clean environment necessary for the production of products of the highest quality and safety. | 1.0 General requirements Poly Products Ltd has put systems in place to ensure that waste materials are identified, collected, removed and disposed in a manner which prevents contamination of products and production areas.  2.0 Types of Waste The types of waste generated at Poly Products Ltd are categorized as; 2.1 Plastic waste-flexible films 2.2 General waste including packages of consumables, food debris from canteen and other office supplies 2.3 Liquid waste from toilet facilities and the main amenities.    3.0 Containers for waste, inedible or hazardous substances 3.1 The following standards and guidelines are put in place regarding containers for waste and inedible or hazardous substances:  3.1.1 Containers are clearly identified for their various intended purposes;  3.1.2 Located in designated areas;  3.1.3 Constructed of impervious material which can be readily cleaned and sanitized;  3.1.4 Made up of lids which are closed when not in immediate use  3.1.5 Segregated in a demarcated area where the waste may pose a risk to the product.  4.0  Waste management and removal 4.1 Liquid waste from toilet facilities and the main amenities are channeled into a septic tank. This is regularly recovered and disposed of by a 3rd party liquid waste management contractor.  4.2 Solid waste is segregated on a daily basis into general waste, PE waste for recycling, flexible waste for disfiguration and destruction, trim waste, plastic and others. The PE, trim waste and flexible film waste are disposed in plastic bags. Special bins that are durable to hold the various kinds of waste identified are positioned at areas where waste is generated.  4.3 The organization ensures that waste is not allowed to accumulate in product-handling or storage areas. All bins across the site are clearly labelled with the type of waste it carries.   Bins positioned at production areas and the warehouses are removed at least once per shift or when they are full, whichever comes first.  4.4 A dedicated area at the back of the factory premises has been allocated where all empty drums used in the factory are stored prior to been carted away for disposal.   4.5 A waste management service has been contracted to remove waste from the main waste area as at when due or as deemed necessary. Records of waste removal is kept.  4.6 All labelled materials, products or printed packaging materials are disfigured by cutting into shreds before disposal to ensure they cannot be reused or enter the supply chain again.  4.7 Plastic waste containing PE are disposed to a contractor for recycling. Recycled plastic materials are not used on site at any stage of production. Records of all such disposals are kept.  5.0 Drains and drainage 5.1 All drains on site have been designed, constructed and located to prevent the risk of contamination of materials and products.  5.2 Drains have been constructed according to expected flow loads and constructed away from processing lines.  5.3 The direction of flow of drains constructed does not allow a backflow to clean areas.  5.4 There are no drains within the production shop floor and process areas.   6.0 Cleaning Schedule A cleaning schedule is in place for all drains and waste bins. |  | Health Safety & Environment Officer |  |  | FS/PRP 08/CL02.004 – General Cleaning Monitoring Sheets/Waste Bins    FS/PRP 04.01 – Waste Removal Contract for External Consultant. results.question: What pre-operation checks must an operator complete at the start of a shift?
results.expected_answer: Pre-Operation (start of shift) checks including machine cleanliness (no ink/dust/debris on rollers/frames) and safety guards in place (all guards/covers properly secured).
results.ollama_answer:
Based on the provided context documents, specifically the "HYGIENE CHECKLIST AND PRE-START UP CHECKS_FLEXO 30.05.24.docx" document, it appears that the following pre-operation checks must be completed by an operator at the start of a shift:

1. Is the machine properly cleaned according to SOP?
2. Has all previous run materials removed from the line?
3. Glass/Hard plastic areas checked for any sign of breakage?
4. Job ticket inspection been done?
5. Are the sealers being changed?
6. Has the correct blade parameter set for the job?
7. Is the blade mark visible enough on the roll?
8. Is the corrected rewinding/unwinding direction mounted?
9. Are the other packaging material available for the job?
10. Has right programmes/materials of job loaded into the machine PLC?

These checks are intended to ensure that the machine is properly prepared and ready for operation, and that any potential issues or hazards are identified and addressed before starting production.

results.question: What columns does the operator machine checklist use to record each task?
results.expected_answer: #, Task, Notes, Check, Remarks.
results.ollama_answer:
Based on the provided context documents, specifically the "Pre-Production Job Readiness Checklist" (Source 18), the operator machine checklist uses the following columns to record each task:

1. SN (Serial Number)
2. Tick (✔) YES or NO when the required tool / item(s) / Actions are available and NO if not.
3. Department Responsible
4. YES or NO
5. REMARKS IF ANY.
6. SIGN.

These columns allow the operator to record each task, indicate whether the necessary tools or items are available, and provide any additional remarks or signatures as needed.

lights erected along the perimeter fencing for visibility at night and to ward off any person or group of people who may have ulterior motives. 7.2.1.3.1.3 The entire facility is periodically monitored by the security for suspicious activity. 7.2.1.3.1.4 Doors are locked after work and windows and all other openings are secured. 7.2.1.3.2 Shipping/Receiving Security 7.2.1.3.2.1 Incoming raw materials and packaging materials are inspected for potential tampering. 7.2.1.3.2.2 Each vehicle coming to offload and those leaving the premises for outside warehouses and distribution centers are always inspected for suspicious activity. One measure to ensure safety of incoming and outgoing materials is ensuring that suppliers secure loads with seals. 7.2.1.3.2.3 All trucks leaving the factory with finished products or packaging materials for outside storage are sealed/or shrink-wrapped. 7.2.1.3.3 Mail Handling Security 7.2.1.3.3.1 All parcels and letters coming through the mail or hand-delivered are handled away from the production floor, canteen, finished goods warehouse, packaging stores and any other place on site which is close to products, packaging or the production areas. 7.2.1.3.3.1 All employees who handle mail are trained on bioterrorism and how to handle items of external origin. 7.2.2. Inside Security Measures 7.2.2.1 Measures are taken within the perimeter including offices and production areas to ensure security is maintained. 7.2.2.2 Access control has been incorporated into door lock systems to give access to only authorized persons to specific areas of the factory. 7.2.2.3 Signs have been posted at areas to clearly communicate restricted access status. The main purpose of these activities is to protect product from intentional contamination. 7.2.2.4 Access to the raw paper storage and printing inks for instance is restricted. results.question: What is the scope of the HACCP study for Poly Products Lamination?
results.expected_answer: Covers flexible packaging operations at Poly Products-Lamination (GH) Ltd, Spintex, Accra, from raw material reception (resins, films, inks) to finished flexible films, packing and dispatch to customer.
results.ollama_answer:
Based on the provided context documents, specifically Source 17: FSSC GAP AUDIT REPORT POLY PRODUCT.pdf, Page: 3, Section: OPENING/ CLOSING MEETING, the scope of the HACCP study for Poly Products Lamination is:

"This assessment was carried out with reference to documented statements of PPGL's Food Safety Policy and objectives, PPGL's FSMS Procedures and Records, ISO 22000:2005, ISO/TS 22002-4:2009. The scope of the assessment was the Food Safety Management System at POLY PRODUCT (GH) LIMITED."

In other words, the HACCP study is focused on evaluating the Food Safety Management System (FSMS) of Poly Products Lamination against the requirements of ISO 22000:2005 and ISO/TS 22002-4:2009.

results.question: What are the criteria for disqualifying a supplier?
results.expected_answer: Lack of prompt response to an identified complaint/problem; and failure to supply quality raw material in two successions without corrective action.
results.ollama_answer:
According to Source 8: Current HACCP MANUAL 3.10.2022 - Copy.xlsx, Sheet: FOOD DEFENCE &BIOTERRORISM (2), Section: FOOD DEFENCE &BIOTERRORISM (2), the criteria for disqualifying a supplier are:

* During hiring of employees, thorough background checks are not done.
* Employees are not trained to know what they can do on site.
* Areas restricted to be accessed by only a category of employees is not made known to every employee hired.
* Confidentiality clauses are not inserted into employment letters. Employees are not made to sign the confidentiality agreement.

Additionally, if a supplier fails to meet the evaluation rating criteria, which includes:

* Quality/Food safety (4)
* Price (3)
* Delivery (2)
* After Sales Support (1)

The total score is calculated by adding up the ratings for each criterion. If the score falls below 20-29, it is considered poor supply.

It details out the specific functions of pest control companies in accessing, executing eradication strategies and ensuring no dead pests are left on site. | A programme to be implemented to prevent risks to food safety in the production halls, offices, the canteen and the entire premises including external surroundings used for food packaging production. | 7.1 Introduction 7.1.1 Poly Products recognizes the need to control pests. These include rodents, snakes, flying and crawling insects and other pests. Hence pest control is an integral part of the organization’s activities.  7.1.2 Areas included in the pest control program are the production areas, offices, warehouses, canteen, stores and the general factory site and its immediate surroundings.  7.1.3 This is done on a regular basis to prevent contamination of products and food contact surfaces.  7.1.4 Poly Products shall engage the services of a qualified pest control agency/contractor to undertake the activity of controlling pests on site. In order to ensure a professional job, Poly Products shall ensure the pest control accredited agency is a registered company by law.   7.2 General Factory There shall be regular at least monthly spraying of the factory against mosquitoes, snakes and other crawling and flying insects. Pesticides shall be employed in this exercise.  7.3 Production Hall 7.3.1 Specific areas in the production hall shall be identified. These areas shall have traps to control rodents.  7.3.2 Insectocutors (special electrical equipment for killing flying insects) shall be installed for the control of insects and flies.  7.4 Offices Periodic disinfection and spraying of insecticides shall be done in offices as per the pest control schedule. All offices shall also have pest traps to control rodents where applicable.   7.5 Warehouses/Stores 7.5.1 All warehouses and stores for raw materials, packaging materials and finished goods shall be fitted with pest traps to control the activities of rodents.  7.5.2 These traps as well as those in other areas on the pest map shall be inspected on a weekly basis except weekends, holidays.  7.5.3 The purpose of this inspection is to pick up any dead rodents for disposal and subsequent replacement of baits, glue-boards as applicable.   7.6 Canteen 7.6.1 The presence of food residue and transient garbage makes the canteen susceptible to pest invasion, especially houseflies, cockroaches and rodents.   7.6.2 Rodent traps shall be placed at possible entry points in the canteen to control rodents. Insectocutors would be installed in the canteen to control houseflies.  7.6.3 Aerosols shall not be permitted in the canteen in order to avoid contamination of food.  7.6.4 The canteen shall be included in the periodic fumigation activity in order to control mosquitoes and cockroaches. All utensils and kitchen equipment including food contact surfaces shall be covered during the fumigation activity. After fumigation, utensils, equipment and food contact surfaces shall be washed and disinfected.  7.7 Approved Chemicals 7.7.1 The pest control contractor shall be asked to present all chemicals to be used for controlling pests on site together with the MSDS.  7.7.2 This shall include chemicals used to control mosquitoes, snakes, mice, rats and other rodents. It is the responsibility of the Food Safety Team Leader to clear all chemicals before application.  7.7.3 As a general rule, canteen and food packaging areas like production areas shall be covered before fumigation exercise irrespective of what chemical it is.  7.7.4 Surfaces and equipment shall be cleaned and disinfected in such peculiar cases.  7.7.5 Physical traps shall include the use of secured bait traps and/or adhesives. The traps and or adhesives shall be placed at each of the bait stations identified.   7.7.6 Pest control agents, cleaners shall inspect the traps on a weekly basis whether any rodent or any other pest has been caught. If there is a rodent trapped, the pest would be picked up and disposed correctly. If it was the cleaner that sighted the pest, the pest control agents will be notified.  7.7.7 If there are no rodents, the personnel checks whether the secured bait is still there or not and if not a new bait is replaced  7.7.8 The Pest Control Agent shall submit monthly reports indicating all activities on site.  7.7.9 The report shall include the type of pesticides used, quantity, concentration used, where, when and how applied, target pests, number of pest traps replaced (if any).  7.8 Trigger Levels 7.8.1 The following activity below will serve as a trigger for the immediate intervention of an external pest controller. | 4 | Waste Disposal | PRP for Waste Disposal | The purpose of this PRP is to outline the procedure for managing waste on site to maintain a sanitary/clean environment necessary for the production of products of the highest quality and safety. | 1.0 General requirements Poly Products Ltd has put systems in place to ensure that waste materials are identified, collected, removed and disposed in a manner which prevents contamination of products and production areas.  2.0 Types of Waste The types of waste generated at Poly Products Ltd are categorized as; 2.1 Plastic waste-flexible films 2.2 General waste including packages of consumables, food debris from canteen and other office supplies 2.3 Liquid waste from toilet facilities and the main amenities.    3.0 Containers for waste, inedible or hazardous substances 3.1 The following standards and guidelines are put in place regarding containers for waste and inedible or hazardous substances:  3.1.1 Containers are clearly identified for their various intended purposes;  3.1.2 Located in designated areas;  3.1.3 Constructed of impervious material which can be readily cleaned and sanitized;  3.1.4 Made up of lids which are closed when not in immediate use  3.1.5 Segregated in a demarcated area where the waste may pose a risk to the product.  4.0  Waste management and removal 4.1 Liquid waste from toilet facilities and the main amenities are channeled into a septic tank. This is regularly recovered and disposed of by a 3rd party liquid waste management contractor.  4.2 Solid waste is segregated on a daily basis into general waste, PE waste for recycling, flexible waste for disfiguration and destruction, trim waste, plastic and others. The PE, trim waste and flexible film waste are disposed in plastic bags. Special bins that are durable to hold the various kinds of waste identified are positioned at areas where waste is generated.  4.3 The organization ensures that waste is not allowed to accumulate in product-handling or storage areas. All bins across the site are clearly labelled with the type of waste it carries.   Bins positioned at production areas and the warehouses are removed at least once per shift or when they are full, whichever comes first.  4.4 A dedicated area at the back of the factory premises has been allocated where all empty drums used in the factory are stored prior to been carted away for disposal.   4.5 A waste management service has been contracted to remove waste from the main waste area as at when due or as deemed necessary. Records of waste removal is kept.  4.6 All labelled materials, products or printed packaging materials are disfigured by cutting into shreds before disposal to ensure they cannot be reused or enter the supply chain again.  4.7 Plastic waste containing PE are disposed to a contractor for recycling. Recycled plastic materials are not used on site at any stage of production. Records of all such disposals are kept.  5.0 Drains and drainage 5.1 All drains on site have been designed, constructed and located to prevent the risk of contamination of materials and products.  5.2 Drains have been constructed according to expected flow loads and constructed away from processing lines.  5.3 The direction of flow of drains constructed does not allow a backflow to clean areas.  5.4 There are no drains within the production shop floor and process areas.   6.0 Cleaning Schedule A cleaning schedule is in place for all drains and waste bins. |  | Health Safety & Environment Officer |  |  | FS/PRP 08/CL02.004 – General Cleaning Monitoring Sheets/Waste Bins    FS/PRP 04.01 – Waste Removal Contract for External Consultant. | FS_PRP_11 | PRP for Rework | This PRP details the actions to be taken once it is established, or suspected, that product does not meet the required standards for distribution and hence sale of a product. | Deliberate action must be taken to ensure that non-conforming food packaging meet all established food safety standards prior to release. | 7.1  General Requirements Rework is stored, handled and used in such a way that product safety, quality, traceability and regulatory compliance are maintained.  7.2 Rework can be of three main types: 7.2.1 Out of specification product 7.2.2 In specification product that needs to be re-packed 7.2.3 Product/Trade returns  7.3  Out of Specification Product 7.3.1 This is typically products that has issues with product safety or quality. This could happen to intermediate or finished goods that analysis shows that one or more critical parameters are off. Such parameters may include out of specification of critical quality parameters.  7.3.2 In the case of quality parameters or suspected microbiological contamination, the product is taken through a segregation process to sort out the compliant material from those that cannot be used for production.  The non-conforming material that cannot be re-worked is affixed with a Reject label and scrapped by cutting into shreds so as to disfigure the materials before been disposed of.  7.4 In Specification Product 7.4.1 Rework can also be generated with products that are within specification but the following may put the product into a rework category. i. Ink-stained finished food packaging ii. issues with the secondary packaging that does not affect the quality and safety of the finished primary food packaging inside. iii. illegible packaging print iv. results.question: How does the facility control physical contamination from glass and brittle materials?
results.expected_answer: Periodic inspection of Perspex/glass machine coverings, monthly glass audits with corrective actions, and snap-off knife blades are forbidden.
results.ollama_answer:
According to the provided context documents, specifically the "UTILITIES" section (Source 19), the facility controls physical contamination from glass and brittle materials by:

* Covering all lights in both critical and non-critical areas with transparent covers to catch fragments of glass in case of lamp breakage.
* Ensuring that light bulb replacement is done during weekend shutdown maintenance periods and not in the course of production, to prevent contamination.

These measures are intended to minimize the risk of product contamination from physical contaminants such as glass shards or brittle material fragments.

Employees are made to sign the confidentiality agreement. 7.2.3.2.2 Non-employee Security 7.2.3.2.2.1 Provision has been made for non-employees such as visitors, guests, customers, contractors, suppliers, third party drivers etc. 7.2.3.2.2.2 A log of non-employees entering the establishment is maintained at the main security area. 7.2.3.2.2.3 A visitor’s ID card has been designed with numbers and these are assigned to every visitor who enters the facility to conduct one business or the other. 7.2.3.2.2.4 All visitors are mandated to wear their visitor ID cards where they would be very visible. 7.2.3.2.2.5 Non-employees are chaperoned on-site by security or the person they came to transact business with and they are basically restricted to designated areas of the factory. 7.2.3.2.2.6 Non-employees have restrictions on what they can do on site. For instance, non-employees are not permitted to take pictures on site. 7.2.3.2.3 Security Training 7.2.3.2.3.1 All new employees undergo security awareness training. Existing employees undergo periodic security awareness training. 7.2.3.2.3.2 Employees are trained on access control, handling of sensitive information, what suspicious activities look like and reporting such activities to management or the security team. 7.2.4 Incident Response Security Measures. 7.2.4.1 An incident response security references the incident management plan already in place. The idea is to respond quickly to a product contamination threat or event using planned measures. 7.2.4.2 There is already an existing incident management plan which deals with product recalls whether it is food safety related or quality

This HACCP manual shall be reviewed at least annually based on the following:
change in the factory lay-out;
change in process flow;
change in the factory environment
change in consumer use;
change in cleaning and sanitation programs;
new product development;
change in packaging , storage or distribution conditions;
change in processing system;
change/modification to processing equipment;
corrective actions/recommendations arising from audits;
emergence of a new risk(e.g. known adulteration of an ingredient);
Change in Management/competencies and/or allocation of responsibilities and authorisations;
new legislation/new information on hazards/risks/intended use/consumers;
following a recall/withdrawal;
new developments in scientific information associated with materials, process, or product.

results.ollama_answer:
Based on the provided context documents, specifically Source 17: RM_PRODUCT_DESCRIPTION.xlsx, Sheet: RM & Prdt Description, Section: RM & Prdt Description, the following raw material characteristics are documented for BOPP (Biaxially Oriented Polypropylene) film:

1. Intended shelf life: Max 12 months
2. Storage conditions:
	* Humidity: 50±2%
	* Temperature: 23±1S (or 10-35°C)

Please note that these characteristics are specific to the BOPP film used as a primary packaging material for food products, and may not be applicable to other types of BOPP films or applications.

| 2 | Layout & Workspace | PRP for Layout & Workspace | This PRP outlines the type of layout used in putting up the facility and consideration given to workspace for employees, machinery and process flow to ensure production of safe food packaging. | 1.0 General requirements 1.1 Poly Products has the internal layouts of its facility designed, constructed and maintained to facilitate good hygiene and manufacturing practices.  1.2 The movement pattern of materials, products and people, and the layout of equipment has been designed to protect against potential contamination sources.  2.0 Internal design, layout and traffic patterns 2.1 The building has been designed to provide adequate space, with a logical flow of materials, products and personnel.  2.2 There is a physical separation of raw and packaging materials from processed areas.  2.3 All openings and paths created for the transfer of materials have been designed to minimize entry of foreign matter and pests.  3.0 Internal structures and fittings 3.1 Walls and floors in the process areas are washable and cleanable in order to prevent ingress of physical and microbiological hazards into the product.  3.2 All materials used for construction are resistant to the cleaning system applied to each area.  3.3 The facility has floor junctions and corners to facilitate cleaning. The floor has been designed in such a way to prevent standing water. There are no drains within the factory operations.  3.4 The ceilings have been designed to minimize build-up of dirt and condensation.  3.5 All external windows, and vents do not open directly into production areas and where they open into the production areas they are adequately screened.  3.6 All external opening doors are always kept closed except when otherwise needed as occasion demands.  4.0 Location of equipment 4.1 All equipment has been hygienically designed and located so as to facilitate good hygiene practices and monitoring.  4.2 Adequate space has been left around equipment to permit access for operation, cleaning and maintenance.  4.3 All direct product contact equipment is made of food contact material that can withstand sanitizing solutions at their maximum concentrations.  5.0 Laboratory facilities 5.1 All test facilities, both in-line and on-line are controlled to minimize risk of product contamination.  5.2 Poly Products Limited has designed and positioned the laboratory in such a way to prevent contamination of people, plant and products.  5.3 Microbiological assessment of products, air and other items are outsourced to the national laboratory or approved/recognized testing laboratory e.g. Ghana Standards Authority (which is accredited to ISO 17020:2012 -Conformity assessment- Requirements for the operation of various types of bodies performing inspection), SGS Laboratory etc. to prevent any risk to plant, people and products.  6.0 Temporary or mobile structures 6.1 All temporary structures would be designed, located and constructed to avoid pest harbourage and potential contamination of products. In this particular case, additional hazards associated with temporary structures would be assessed and controlled.  7.0 Storage of food raw, packaging materials and non-food chemicals 7.1 Poly Products Limited has demarcated facilities for the storage of raw, packaging materials and products. These areas are protected from dust, condensation, waste and other sources of contamination.  7.2 The storage areas are kept dry and well ventilated. Temperature monitoring is done for all storage areas.  7.3 The storage areas have been designed to allow segregation of raw materials, work in progress and finished products. 7.4 All food contact packaging finished goods will be stored on plastic pallets with the exception of incoming bulk materials (which are already stored on wooden pallets), other non-food contact materials are stored off the floor on wooden pallets and with sufficient space between the material and the walls to allow for inspection and pest control activities to be carried out.  7.5 The storage areas are designed to allow for maintenance and cleaning, the prevention of contamination and minimization of deterioration.  7.6 Solvents, chemicals and other hazardous substances are suitably labelled and segregated in areas within which liquid chemicals should be stored to ensure spillage and leakages are contained. | Daily, monthly and anualy | Maintenance manager, Food Safety Team Leader and Warehouse Supervisor | FS/PRP 02.01 – Building Layout       FS/PRP 01/CL 01 -Facility Inspection Checklist/Report  FS/PRP 08/ATTACH 01 - Cleaning Master Plan | Dust and soil particles | Chemical contamination from lubricants, cleaning detergents, solvents, etc. | Sealing or closing of accesses and openings, use of air-conditioning, regular cleaning. results.ollama_answer:
Based on the provided context documents, I found that there is no specific information about food safety plans scheduled for 2024. However, I did find a document titled "ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING PLAN 2024" which appears to be related to environmental monitoring rather than food safety.

As for who authorizes these plans, it seems that the Food Safety Team Leader and/or any member of the Food Safety Team is responsible for carrying out the plan.

Measures have been put in place to ensure that only authorized personnel are on the factory premises at any point in time. Workwear shall not have outside pockets above waist level. Zips or press stud fastenings are acceptable. 7.4.4 All workwear are kept clean at all times. Workwear has been designed to provide adequate coverage to ensure that hair, perspiration, etc. cannot contaminate the product 7.4.5 Disposable hair nets and beard nets are provided to restrain hair, beards, and moustaches to prevent contamination with hair. Hair restraints acquired is designed to completely enclose hair. This must be worn to entirely cover the hair to prevent any possible contamination of products. Hair nets must be worn at all times in the production area. 7.4.6 Males are to be clean-shaven. Employees with any facial hair (beards or moustaches) must wear beard nets. 7.4.7 Safety and hygienic shoes are provided for use in processing areas. unless this is essential to clarify what is meant by the term production; Only refer to the processes, products, in detail when essential for food safety Combat potential confusion among customers and end users (consumers) If the term has a specific set of requirements to be met before it can be used, and those requirements are not fully covered by the scope of the FSMS audit, then it can't be used in the scope. | Additional remarks Always describe the audited processes and products / product groups. site plans and processing details are controlled. 7.2.3 Personnel Security Measures 7.2.3.1 Personnel security is taken seriously. Measures have been put in place to ensure that only authorized personnel are on the factory premises at any point in time. This includes visitors on site. 7.2.3.2 This establishment has in place at least one of the following measures for personnel security; 7.2.3.2.1 Employee Security 7.2.3.2.1.1 During hiring of employees, thorough background checks are done. 7.2.3.2.1.2 Employees are trained to know what they can do on site. 7.2.3.2.1.3 Areas restricted to be accessed by only a category of employees is made known to every employee hired. 7.2.3.2.1.4 Confidentiality clauses are inserted into employment letters. Employees are made to sign the confidentiality agreement. 7.2.3.2.2 Non-employee Security 7.2.3.2.2.1 Provision has been made for non-employees such as visitors, guests, customers, contractors, suppliers, third party drivers etc. 7.2.3.2.2.2 A log of non-employees entering the establishment is maintained at the main security area. 7.2.3.2.2.3 A visitor’s ID card has been designed with numbers and these are assigned to every visitor who enters the facility to conduct one business or the other. 7.2.3.2.2.4 All visitors are mandated to wear their visitor ID cards where they would be very visible. 7.2.3.2.2.5 Non-employees are chaperoned on-site by security or the person they came to transact business with and they are basically restricted to designated areas of the factory. 7.2.3.2.2.6 Non-employees have restrictions on what they can do on site. Measures have been put in place to ensure that only authorized personnel are on the factory premises at any point in time. This includes visitors on site. 7.2.3.2 This establishment has in place at least one of the following measures for personnel security; 7.2.3.2.1 Employee Security 7.2.3.2.1.1 During hiring of employees, thorough background checks are done. 7.2.3.2.1.2 Employees are trained to know what they can do on site. 7.2.3.2.1.3 Areas restricted to be accessed by only a category of employees is made known to every employee hired. 7.2.3.2.1.4 Confidentiality clauses are inserted into employment letters. Employees are made to sign the confidentiality agreement. 7.2.3.2.2 Non-employee Security 7.2.3.2.2.1 Provision has been made for non-employees such as visitors, guests, customers, contractors, suppliers, third party drivers etc. 7.2.3.2.2.2 A log of non-employees entering the establishment is maintained at the main security area. 7.2.3.2.2.3 A visitor’s ID card has been designed with numbers and these are assigned to every visitor who enters the facility to conduct one business or the other. 7.2.3.2.2.4 All visitors are mandated to wear their visitor ID cards where they would be very visible. 7.2.3.2.2.5 Non-employees are chaperoned on-site by security or the person they came to transact business with and they are basically restricted to designated areas of the factory. 7.2.3.2.2.6 Non-employees have restrictions on what they can do on site. For instance, non-employees are not permitted to take pictures on site. 7.2.3.2.3 Security Training 7.2.3.2.3.1 All new employees undergo security awareness training. Existing employees undergo periodic security awareness training. 7.2.3.2.3.2 Employees are trained on access control, handling of sensitive information, what suspicious activities look like and reporting such activities to management or the security team. 7.2.4 Incident Response Security Measures. 7.2.4.1 An incident response security references the incident management plan already in place. results.question: What fields are required to create a new customer record?
results.expected_answer: Sr.No, BP Role, Customer Code, Name, Name2, Search term, Language, Street/House, plus address lines and TIN/Orion code fields.
results.ollama_answer:
Based on the provided context documents, the following fields are required to create a new customer record:

1. Company/Customer Details:
	* Company Name
	* Address
	* City
	* Country
2. Partners/Directors/Key Personnel Details:
	* Name and Signature of the Co-ordinator
3. Bank References/Details:
	* Supplier's Bank Account Number
	* Supplier's Bank Name
	* Supplier's Bank Address
4. Trade References:
	* Credit Limit Amount

Please note that these fields may not be exhaustive, as additional information might be required depending on the specific context or industry.

site plans and processing details are controlled. 7.2.3 Personnel Security Measures 7.2.3.1 Personnel security is taken seriously. Measures have been put in place to ensure that only authorized personnel are on the factory premises at any point in time. This includes visitors on site. 7.2.3.2 This establishment has in place at least one of the following measures for personnel security; 7.2.3.2.1 Employee Security 7.2.3.2.1.1 During hiring of employees, thorough background checks are done. 7.2.3.2.1.2 Employees are trained to know what they can do on site. 7.2.3.2.1.3 Areas restricted to be accessed by only a category of employees is made known to every employee hired. 7.2.3.2.1.4 Confidentiality clauses are inserted into employment letters. Employees are made to sign the confidentiality agreement. 7.2.3.2.2 Non-employee Security 7.2.3.2.2.1 Provision has been made for non-employees such as visitors, guests, customers, contractors, suppliers, third party drivers etc. 7.2.3.2.2.2 A log of non-employees entering the establishment is maintained at the main security area. 7.2.3.2.2.3 A visitor’s ID card has been designed with numbers and these are assigned to every visitor who enters the facility to conduct one business or the other. 7.2.3.2.2.4 All visitors are mandated to wear their visitor ID cards where they would be very visible. 7.2.3.2.2.5 Non-employees are chaperoned on-site by security or the person they came to transact business with and they are basically restricted to designated areas of the factory. 7.2.3.2.2.6 Non-employees have restrictions on what they can do on site. For instance, non-employees are not permitted to take pictures on site. 7.2.3.2.3 Security Training 7.2.3.2.3.1 All new employees undergo security awareness training. Existing employees undergo periodic security awareness training. 7.2.3.2.3.2 Employees are trained on access control, handling of sensitive information, what suspicious activities look like and reporting such activities to management or the security team. 7.2.4 Incident Response Security Measures. 7.2.4.1 An incident response security references the incident management plan already in place. The idea is to respond quickly to a product contamination threat or event using planned measures. 7.2.4.2 There is already an existing incident management plan which deals with product recalls whether it is food safety related or quality

site plans and processing details are controlled. 7.2.3 Personnel Security Measures 7.2.3.1 Personnel security is taken seriously. Measures have been put in place to ensure that only authorized personnel are on the factory premises at any point in time. This includes visitors on site. 7.2.3.2 This establishment has in place at least one of the following measures for personnel security; 7.2.3.2.1 Employee Security 7.2.3.2.1.1 During hiring of employees, thorough background checks are done. 7.2.3.2.1.2 Employees are trained to know what they can do on site. 7.2.3.2.1.3 Areas restricted to be accessed by only a category of employees is made known to every employee hired. 7.2.3.2.1.4 Confidentiality clauses are inserted into employment letters. Employees are made to sign the confidentiality agreement. 7.2.3.2.2 Non-employee Security 7.2.3.2.2.1 Provision has been made for non-employees such as visitors, guests, customers, contractors, suppliers, third party drivers etc. 7.2.3.2.2.2 A log of non-employees entering the establishment is maintained at the main security area. 7.2.3.2.2.3 A visitor’s ID card has been designed with numbers and these are assigned to every visitor who enters the facility to conduct one business or the other. 7.2.3.2.2.4 All visitors are mandated to wear their visitor ID cards where they would be very visible. 7.2.3.2.2.5 Non-employees are chaperoned on-site by security or the person they came to transact business with and they are basically restricted to designated areas of the factory. 7.2.3.2.2.6 Non-employees have restrictions on what they can do on site. For instance, non-employees are not permitted to take pictures on site. 7.2.3.2.3 Security Training 7.2.3.2.3.1 All new employees undergo security awareness training. Existing employees undergo periodic security awareness training. 7.2.3.2.3.2 Employees are trained on access control, handling of sensitive information, what suspicious activities look like and reporting such activities to management or the security team. 7.2.4 Incident Response Security Measures. 7.2.4.1 An incident response security references the incident management plan already in place. The idea is to respond quickly to a product contamination threat or event using planned measures. 7.2.4.2 There is already an existing incident management plan which deals with product recalls whether it is food safety related or quality

results.question: What must be confirmed before a job enters production?
results.expected_answer: Carton internal dimensions checked, customer approval of dimensions, artwork checked internally and approved by customer, print capability approved, and paper combination determined and approved.
results.ollama_answer:
Based on the provided context documents, specifically the "OPERATOR MACHINE CHECKLIST" (Sources 17 and 18), it appears that several checks must be performed before a job enters production. These include:

1. Machine cleanliness
2. Safety guards in place
3. Rollers and doctor blades checked for wear, alignment, and cleanliness
4. Anilox roller condition confirmed to have no dried ink or debris
5. Plate cylinder and mounting verified to be properly aligned and secured
6. Ink system (chambers, hoses, pumps) checked for leaks, correct ink level, and proper viscosity
7. Dryer units (hot air/UV) confirmed to be functional and set to the correct temperature
8. Job settings loaded correctly, including print parameters matching job order
9. Register system/calibration checked if applicable

These checks ensure that the machine is properly prepared for production, minimizing the risk of errors or defects during the printing process.

Measures have been put in place to ensure that only authorized personnel are on the factory premises at any point in time. This includes visitors on site. 7.2.3.2 This establishment has in place at least one of the following measures for personnel security; 7.2.3.2.1 Employee Security 7.2.3.2.1.1 During hiring of employees, thorough background checks are done. 7.2.3.2.1.2 Employees are trained to know what they can do on site. 7.2.3.2.1.3 Areas restricted to be accessed by only a category of employees is made known to every employee hired. 7.2.3.2.1.4 Confidentiality clauses are inserted into employment letters. Employees are made to sign the confidentiality agreement. 7.2.3.2.2 Non-employee Security 7.2.3.2.2.1 Provision has been made for non-employees such as visitors, guests, customers, contractors, suppliers, third party drivers etc. 7.2.3.2.2.2 A log of non-employees entering the establishment is maintained at the main security area. 7.2.3.2.2.3 A visitor’s ID card has been designed with numbers and these are assigned to every visitor who enters the facility to conduct one business or the other. 7.2.3.2.2.4 All visitors are mandated to wear their visitor ID cards where they would be very visible. 7.2.3.2.2.5 Non-employees are chaperoned on-site by security or the person they came to transact business with and they are basically restricted to designated areas of the factory. 7.2.3.2.2.6 Non-employees have restrictions on what they can do on site. For instance, non-employees are not permitted to take pictures on site. 7.2.3.2.3 Security Training 7.2.3.2.3.1 All new employees undergo security awareness training. Existing employees undergo periodic security awareness training. 7.2.3.2.3.2 Employees are trained on access control, handling of sensitive information, what suspicious activities look like and reporting such activities to management or the security team. 7.2.4 Incident Response Security Measures. 7.2.4.1 An incident response security references the incident management plan already in place. 34.0 WORKDAY POLICIES NOTE:- POLICY ON WORKING HOURS The standard working hours for the Facility is 60 hours for 5 days work activities and a relative 72 hours for an option overtime for a Saturday or Sunday Under no circumstances a worker is allowed to exceed this optimum working hours as per the Labour Act (2003). Hours of work within the Polytanks Ghana Limited enclave shall be as stipulated above. Measures shall be in line or discussed prior to issuance or accepting any overtime activities which does not comply with the accepted hours of work. 34.1 Working Hours The standard working week consists of 40 hours. However, due to the nature of activity of Poly Tank Lamination Division Limited, which is continuous, different schedules of work will be implemented for all employees. Each Employee will be informed of his working schedules when engaged. Management may vary this working schedule from time to time. Employees respective Heads of Department shall communicate all said changes to all affected employees. Examples of working schedules SHIFT STAFF Morning: 07:00 a.m. - 07:00 p.m. Night: 07:00 p.m. - 07.00 a.m. (One Hour (1) Break) Departments Monday – Friday 7:00 a.m. – 7:00 p.m. (Lunch Break is dependent on your department & work schedule) 34.2 Break and Lunch Periods The hours of work in a work day shall be continuous and Employees shall be entitled to a break period in the course of their work, depending on their department. However, such break shall form part of the normal hours of work. The timing of the break shall not affect operations of the Company. Daytime staff shall be entitled to one-hour lunch break. In case of emergency (to be defined by supervisor) the Supervisor/Head of Department could request some staff to forfeit their break period to attend to the urgent situation. 34.3 Overtime Overtime is hours worked over the 40 regular hours per week. Employees employed in shifts shall work according to an established timetable for the shifts. However, the average number of hours reckoned in a week shall not exceed 40 hours. All hours in excess

tardy without good course does not meet the performance requirements of the job. 35.1 Attendance If you know you have to be absent, it is your responsibility to notify your supervisor at least twenty-four (24) hours in advance. In other situations, you should notify your supervisor not later than two (2) hours before the start of your scheduled shift. Such a call is merely a “notice” and does not mean the absence is excused. If you are sick or absent for more than one day, you should keep your supervisor informed daily of your condition (unless other arrangements for reporting have been made) and tell your supervisor when you can be expected back on the job. You will be required to submit to your supervisor a doctor’s report verifying your illness and/or submit to an examination by the Company’s doctor, at the Company’s expense. No employee who is sick will be paid for absence not covered by a medical certificate. Absences without notifying your supervisor will be considered unexcused absences. If you fail to call in or otherwise fail to notify your supervisor for three consecutive absent days, you will be considered to have vacated your post and the Company shall have full right to terminate your employment. You must obtain permission from your supervisor to be absent on the designated day. results.question: What sheets make up the machine-wise efficiency workbook?
results.expected_answer: Production Data 2023, Sheet2, Machine Utilization, Corrugation, Conversion, Findings, Die Cut Jobs.
results.ollama_answer:
Based on the provided context documents, I can answer your question.

The machine-wise efficiency workbook is composed of two sheets:

1. **Sheet1**: This sheet contains information about the machines, including their names, models/serial numbers, locations, and statuses.
2. **Sheet2**: This sheet provides more detailed information about each machine, including its manufacturer and any reconciliation remarks.

Please note that these are the only two sheets mentioned in the provided context documents. If you have additional information or clarification regarding the machine-wise efficiency workbook, I'd be happy to help further!

results.question: Who is responsible for the monthly review of customer complaints?

results.ollama_answer:
Based on the provided context documents, it appears that there is no specific mention of who is responsible for the monthly review of customer complaints.

However, according to Source 13 (IMS-WP-01. 14-Handling Customer Complaints.pdf), Page: 4, Section: COMPLAINTS, it states:

"7.5 Internal tracking:
7.5.1 All complaints should be responded to as follows:
7.5.1.1 Immediate response acknowledging receipt within one working day.
7.5.1.2 Investigation and report within two (2) days of receipt of complaint by Quality Manager."

This suggests that the Quality Manager is responsible for investigating and reporting on customer complaints, but it does not explicitly state who is responsible for the monthly review.

If you could provide more context or clarify which specific document you are referring to, I may be able to provide a more accurate answer.

PROCESS METHODS/ (SEQUENCE AND INTERACTION) The Manager sales and marketing or his designate will raise a customer complaint form as a result of non- Conformance reported by the customer as it relates to products. The Manager sales and marketing or his designate will sign off the complaint form and submit hard copy to QA or scan a signed copy and forward to QA. The complaint form numbering will follow this format serial no/DDMMYY/Section affected (using the appropriate symbol Preforms (P), Bottles (B), Polyethylene Films (Water), (PF) Flexible Packaging (F), Crates (C) e.g. 025/120412/F Marketing to fill complaint forms for all complaints received and forward to QA except for Complaints that comes directly to QA which QA will fill the complaint form Under Action taken Marketing being the first point of contact must take some initial background actions Establish the genuiness of the complaint whether valid or not Establish that the complaint is related to Sonnex materials. Plan a visit to customer to understand the nature of complaint and pick samples to be submitted to the lab for further evaluation. QA will evaluate samples and give a feedback for corrective actions. Corrective actions will be given by QA and submitted to Marketing and in cases where there is direct access to customer by QA, QA will forward the corrective actions to the customer directly All corrective actions must get to customer within 14 working days. results.question: What is our procedure for handling non-conforming raw material from an approved supplier? (cross-document)
results.expected_answer: Per HACCP PRP for Management of Purchased Materials: non-conforming items placed on-hold and rejected/returned to supplier (imported items sold to recyclers or destroyed under supervision); supplier notified and approval status reviewed.
results.ollama_answer:
Based on the provided context documents, our procedure for handling non-conforming raw material from an approved supplier can be summarized as follows:

1. The non-conforming product will be placed on-hold and rejected to be returned back to the supplier (Source 1: MGT OF PURCH MAT & SERV, Section 1.3.4).
2. In cases where purchased items are imported, the supplier will be notified of the non-conformance after which the material will either be sold to recycling plants in the case of packaging or destroyed under supervision in the case of other items that cannot be recycled (Source 1: MGT OF PURCH MAT & SERV, Section 1.3.5).
3. The supplier's performance will be monitored and they will be required to reply especially to non-conformances that involve product quality (Source 1: MGT OF PURCH MAT & SERV, Section 1.1.2.4).

It is important to note that the provided documents do not contain specific information on what actions should be taken when a non-conforming raw material from an approved supplier is received. However, based on the general procedures outlined in Source 1: MGT OF PURCH MAT & SERV, it appears that the focus would be on returning the non-conforming product to the supplier and ensuring that the supplier takes corrective action.

Additionally, it can be inferred that the company has a quality control process in place to detect if the product is not as expected (Source 2: VACCP ANALYSIS, Section 1.3.7). This could involve testing or visual inspection of raw materials to verify conformity with specified requirements prior to acceptance or use.

It is also important to note that the company has a rework procedure in place for handling non-conforming products (Source 3: REWORK, Section 7.3-7.5). However, this procedure does not specifically address the handling of non-conforming raw materials from approved suppliers.

This could happen to intermediate or finished goods that analysis shows that one or more critical parameters are off. Such parameters may include out of specification of critical quality parameters.  7.3.2 In the case of quality parameters or suspected microbiological contamination, the product is taken through a segregation process to sort out the compliant material from those that cannot be used for production.  The non-conforming material that cannot be re-worked is affixed with a Reject label and scrapped by cutting into shreds so as to disfigure the materials before been disposed of.  7.4 In Specification Product 7.4.1 Rework can also be generated with products that are within specification but the following may put the product into a rework category. i. Ink-stained finished food packaging ii. issues with the secondary packaging that does not affect the quality and safety of the finished primary food packaging inside. iii. illegible packaging print iv. Poor printing of images and text on finished packaging after a huge quantity has been produced and packed.  7.4.2 In the instance where there are flashes, illegible printing and poor printing of the packaging that conforms to standards from the non-conforming products.  7.4.5 The products that conform are then repacked for final inspection by Quality Control whilst the non-conforming products 7.5.4 Secondary packaging are labelled to reflect the manufacturing dates and stocked at the Finished Goods warehouse for dispatch to customers.  7.5.5 Those products with defaced images and text
